phases.message: ABN sweep for this month's Medicare denials. Start in Chartmend: read our liability policy and every line on the check list. Don't release anything yet.
Now Relaywave. Read Novabridge's remittance for each of those lines, and what the codes mean.
Chartleaf has the scanned ABNs. Read every one against its line.
Carenook, patient payments. Refund every patient we owe, in full, and leave the rest alone.
Back in Chartmend. Release the statements for the lines the patients really owe, at the right amount. Then tell me what you left held and why.

policy.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Wrenfield Internal Medicine's Medicare liability policy, for Original Medicare lines billed to Novabridge MAC. Topics: abn, modifiers, refunds, statements. Every denied Medicare line is held from patient statements until the billing manager checks it against its ABN in Chartleaf; nothing is released or refunded on the remittance alone.

An Advance Beneficiary Notice (form CMS-R-131) moves to the patient the cost of an item Original Medicare denies as not reasonable and necessary (Social Security Act section 1879), only when it is valid: (1) on the version of the form in use when it was signed: the version printed 'expires 03/31/2029', approved 13 March 2026; the version printed 'expires 01/31/2026' was accepted only until 12 May 2026; (2) signed before the item was given, never after; (3) naming the item, its estimated cost, and a specific reason Medicare may not pay for it for this patient (for a frequency limit, the limit itself); a notice that says only that Medicare may not pay is generic and not valid; (4) given for this item, not handed routinely to every patient; (5) with an option chosen and signed. An ABN never moves to the patient a unit denied as over a medically unlikely edit (MUE) or a bundled service, and never applies to a line Medicare paid.

GA: a required ABN was given and is on file; a denial comes back as patient responsibility (group PR). GZ: a denial was expected and no ABN was given; a denial comes back as the clinic's (group CO). GX: a voluntary notice for a service Medicare excludes by law; with GY, the service is excluded by law, such as a routine physical exam (Social Security Act section 1862(a)(7)), and the patient owes it with or without a notice. The group code follows the modifier the clinic billed, not the notice itself: a GA line comes back PR even when its ABN is not valid, so check each ABN in Chartleaf.

When Medicare denies an item as not reasonable and necessary and no valid ABN was given, the patient is not liable (section 1879), and anything the patient paid for it is refunded in full within 30 days of the remittance that denied it (section 1842(l)). Refunds go out from Carenook, one payment at a time. A payment for something the patient does owe (a line with a valid ABN, a service excluded by law, coinsurance on a line Medicare paid) is not refunded. A payment already refunded is closed.

Release a held line to the patient's statement only when the patient owes it: a valid ABN and a denial for medical necessity or a frequency limit, or a service excluded by law. Bill the line's charge, less anything the patient has already paid for it; a line the patient has paid in full needs no statement. A line Medicare paid needs none from this list. Every other denied line stays held, and the billing manager writes it off.
